## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU and I/O stall-pressure thresholds to reflect real PSI stall data now that `/proc/pressure` parsing works, so the pressure diagnosis fires on genuine contention instead of staying green until the host is near-dead.

## Problem statement

`cpu_pressure` (warning 70 / critical 85, `some` avg10) and `io_pressure` (warning 50 / critical 80, `full` avg10) were inherited from the pre-parser-fix configuration and have never been validated against real stall data. The IO threshold is worse than unvalidated: a 50 % `full`-line stall is effectively never reached, so `io_pressure` stays permanently green even under genuine I/O starvation — the exact signal the PSI work (SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW) was meant to surface.

## Users

- **Operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`** — "As an operator, I want the before-table pressure rows to flag real CPU contention and I/O starvation at levels my multi-agent host actually reaches, so I am told about a problem while it is still actionable."
- **Agent triaging a slow host** — "As an agent, I want `analyze_pressures()` to surface an actionable pressure with contributors when the host is genuinely starved, instead of skipping a permanently-green `io_pressure` row."
- **Skill maintainer** — "As a maintainer, I want the calibrated values consistent across `config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS` and `SKILL.md`, with boundary tests, so a future parser change cannot silently re-introduce the silence."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `cpu_pressure` is calibrated to **warning 30 / critical 60** (`some` avg10) and `io_pressure` to **warning 5 / critical 20** (`full` avg10) in `config.yaml` and `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, mirroring the `memory_pressure` full-line calibration for IO.
- **AC2** — Calibration is validated against real stall data: the archived busy-host observations (CPU `some` avg10 = 11.58 at load 11.92 on 16 cores → `low`; CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 at load ~44 → `critical`) classify as expected, and **at least one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample** is captured (e.g. a short `dd`/write burst) showing a numeric IO `full` value that currently stays green under 50/80, with the sample and classification recorded in a comment on this item.
- **AC3** — Unit tests cover the new classification boundaries for both metrics: cpu `some` 29.9 → `low`, 30.0 → `warning`, 60.0 → `critical`; io `full` 4.9 → `low`, 5.0 → `warning`, 20.0 → `critical` — replacing the old 70/85 and 50/80 boundary assertions.
- **AC4** — `config.yaml` comments and `SKILL.md` document the new values, their `some`/`full` line basis, the observed-data provenance (including the induced IO sample), and why the IO warning never fired under 50/80. `SKILL.md`'s "Threshold provenance" paragraph is updated to state the validated values rather than "not yet validated".
- **AC5** — All related documentation in this repository is updated: `config.yaml` comments, `config.py` docstrings/comments, `SKILL.md` metric table and provenance section, plus any code comments in `metrics.py` that reference the thresholds. This skill has no README or docs-site entry, so no other documentation surface needs an update.
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — calibration basis:** the archived samples (11.58 busy / 88.78 extreme) plus one induced IO sample bracket realistic stall ranges on this 16-core multi-agent host; other hosts (fewer/more cores, different workloads) can still override per-host values in `config.yaml`.
- **Risk — false amber at 30 % CPU `some`-stall:** a heavily loaded-but-healthy multi-agent host can briefly cross 30 % `some` (at least one task stalled) during test-suite bursts; acceptable — it is the honest stall signal, and `some` semantics are designed to fire early.
- **Risk — induced IO sample disturbs the live host:** the bounded burst must be short and small (e.g. a few hundred MB write/read) so it does not itself cause a false-positive pressure reading on a busy host; time it outside the brief write window.
- **Risk — doc drift:** three surfaces (`config.yaml`, `config.py::_DEFAULTS`, `SKILL.md`) must stay in lock-step; AC4/AC5 and the existing `test_shipped_config_matches_defaults` guard this.
- **Scope-creep risk:** adjacent recalibration ideas (e.g. load-average multipliers vs. PSI, per-host dynamic thresholds) are recorded as linked work items, not folded into this item.

## Impact

Operators now get honest CPU and I/O stall alarms at levels a real multi-agent host reaches — CPU contention flagged at 30 % `some`-stall and genuine I/O starvation at 5 % `full`-stall — instead of a metric that stays green until the box is thrashing.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** threshold values + consistent config/docs/tests + one bounded controlled I/O-stall sample for validation. No parser, line-selection, metric-key, or action behaviour changes.
- **Stable metric keys:** `cpu_pressure` / `io_pressure` must not change (consumed by `pressure_analysis._PRESSURE_METRICS` and the before/after table).
- **Classification semantics:** `classify_metric` is inclusive at the warning/critical lower bounds (`value >= critical` → critical, `value >= warning` → warning); boundary tests assert exactly those edges.
- **Line bases unchanged:** cpu → `some`, io → `full` (decided in SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW); no fallback on missing lines.
- **No new dependencies**; stdlib/unittest only.
- **Repo boundary:** changes land in `skill/machine-hygiene` in this repo (worktree), never the installed global copy by hand.

## Existing state

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py::_DEFAULTS` — `cpu_pressure: warning 70 / critical 85`; `io_pressure: warning 50 / critical 80`.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — same values, with comments claiming ">70 % indicates moderate CPU contention" (70 % `some`-stall is far past moderate) and ">50 % I/O stalled — noticeable slowdown" (never reached on `full`).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" says cpu/io thresholds "have not yet been validated against real stall data".
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — asserts the 70/85 and 50/80 defaults and file-override behaviour.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries` (69.9/70/85) and `test_io_pressure_boundaries` (49.9/50/80) lock in the old values.
- Real observed data: CPU `some` avg10 = 88.78 (2026-09-27, load ~44/16 cores) and 11.58 (2026-10-21 discovery, load 11.92); IO `full` avg10 = 0.00–0.05 (idle observations only — no busy IO sample yet).

## Desired change

1. `_DEFAULTS` and `config.yaml`: `cpu_pressure` → 30/60 (`some` avg10); `io_pressure` → 5/20 (`full` avg10, mirroring `memory_pressure`).
2. Update comments: cpu description corrected to "(moderate CPU contention)" at 30 %; io description explains `full`-line stall % semantics and that 50/80 never fired.
3. Update `SKILL.md` provenance paragraph with the calibrated values, the archived and induced sample evidence, and the rationale.
4. Update boundary tests in `test_metrics.py` and default tests in `test_config.py` to the new values.
5. Validation run: capture a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample (write/read burst, a few seconds), render the `io_pressure` classification under the new thresholds, and paste the sample + classification into a comment on this item.

## Key Files

- `skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` cpu_pressure/io_pressure values (and any threshold-referencing comments).
- `skill/machine-hygiene/config.yaml` — cpu_pressure/io_pressure blocks, warning/critical values and explaining comments.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/SKILL.md` — "Threshold provenance" paragraph and any metric-table threshold notes.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_config.py` — default-value and file-override assertions for cpu/io pressure.
- `skill/machine-hygiene/tests/test_metrics.py` — `test_cpu_pressure_boundaries`, `test_io_pressure_boundaries` and the `collect_metrics` pressure assertions.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW** (completed) — PSI parser fix; this item's `discovered-from` source; established `some`/`full` line selection and the `memory_pressure` 5/20 calibration precedent.
- **WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY** (ContextHub, completed) — threshold miscalibration for multi-agent hosts (process/thread/swap); adjacent calibration work, shipped.
- **WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ** (ContextHub, open) — duplicate proposed-actions table/actions; same discovery session, independent defect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: `cpu_pressure` calibration target (`some` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) keep 70/85, validate + document; (B) lower to warn 30 / crit 60 to catch contention earlier; (C) middle ground (warn 50 / crit 75).
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — 70 % `some`-stall means the host is already severely degraded; an amber band from ~30 % lets the skill propose renice/kill remediation while the host is still responsive.
  - Evidence: real CPU `some` avg10 samples of 11.58 (busy, load 11.92) and 88.78 (extreme, load ~44) on 16-core hosts; current 70/85 classifies the former `low` and the latter `critical`.
- **Q2: `io_pressure` calibration target (`full` avg10)?**
  - Options: (A) mirror memory_pressure warn 5 / crit 20 (same full-line semantics); (B) slightly higher (10/30); (C) keep 50/80 but document.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A**. **Recommended:** A — identical `full`-line semantics and an established 5/20 precedent; keeps the genuine I/O-starvation signal without false alarms at idle.
  - Evidence: observed IO `full` avg10 values are 0.00–0.05; 50/80 was never reachable so the metric stayed green under genuine I/O starvation.
- **Q3: validation data sufficiency (AC1)?**
  - Options: (A) archive observations + live `/proc/pressure` only; (B) also induce a bounded controlled I/O-stall sample.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **B**. **Recommended:** B — AC1 explicitly demands validation against observed busy-host stall percentages, and IO currently has zero busy samples; one bounded induced sample makes calibration evidence-based rather than assumed.
  - Evidence: no archived IO `full` sample exceeds 0.05; a short `dd`/write burst provides the missing busy data point.

No open questions remain.
data.title: machine-hygiene: recalibrate cpu_pressure/io_pressure thresholds now that PSI parsing works

# Intake Brief: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes (SA-0MVNBEPHH009LB5X)

## Problem statement

The refactor skill's auto-fix step reports diagnostics it could not fix as
"Auto-fixed", so a full-project scan can claim 8–9 lint fixes were applied
while `git status` shows the tree is byte-for-byte unchanged. The same
diagnostics are then double-counted under "Remaining smells", eroding trust in
the refactor report.

## Users

Primary user is the **producer / operator** who runs `/skill:refactor`
full-project scans (directly or via scheduled runs) and relies on the report's
"Auto-fixed" and "Remaining smells" counts to judge whether lint debt remains.

- User story 1: **As a** producer running a full-project refactor scan, **I
  want** the "Auto-fixed" count to reflect edits actually written to disk,
  **so that** I trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when
  it was not.
- User story 2: **As a** producer triaging scan output, **I want** unfixable
  diagnostics listed only under "Remaining smells", **so that** the lists are
  not double-counted and I can see exactly what remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` counts a finding as fixed only when the ruff
   entry carries an actual fix: `fix` is non-null **and**
   `fix.applicability == "safe"` (the default scope of `ruff check --fix`
   without `--unsafe-fixes`).
2. `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` counts a message as fixed only when eslint
   indicates a fix was applied (e.g. `output`/`fixed` evidence), or fixes are
   otherwise verified by comparing file content before/after the run.
3. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining
   diagnostics are non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` /
   `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. A regression test proves that a linter run over a file with one safely
   fixable diagnostic reports `Auto-fixed: 1` **and** the file is modified on
   disk.
5. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and**
   reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
6. Unfixed/unsafe diagnostics are surfaced under "Remaining smells
   (non-auto-fixable)" and are never listed in both the auto-fixed list and
   the remaining list for the same run.
7. New/updated unit tests in `tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py` cover the
   fix-detection behaviour, including correcting existing parser fixtures
   (e.g. `test_parse_ruff_fix_output_parses_correctly`, which feeds entries
   with no `fix` payload and currently expects them counted as fixed).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (see the dev-push
   gate).
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   `docs/refactor.md` (the `auto_fix.fixed_findings` / `fixes_applied`
   semantics) and code comments describing the auto-fix step.

## Impact

After this change a refactor scan honestly reports only fixes actually applied
to disk, so producers can trust the "Auto-fixed: N" count and rely on
"Remaining smells" as a non-duplicated list of outstanding diagnostics.

## Constraints

- Ruff's JSON output after `--fix` lists the **remaining** diagnostics; a
  non-null `fix` payload marks a fix that would apply, and
  `fix.applicability == "safe"` is exactly the boundary of what `--fix`
  applies without `--unsafe-fixes`. The refactor pipeline must not add
  `--unsafe-fixes`.
- The change is confined to `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` and its tests
  (`tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py`); no new linter integrations.
- Report output shape (`fixes_applied`, `fixed_findings`,
  `summary.auto_fixed`, the human-readable "Auto-fixed:" line) stays
  consistent so downstream consumers are unchanged.

## Existing state

- `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` converts **every** JSON entry from
  `ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding", ignoring the
  `fix` field — so 9 unfixable diagnostics (EXE005/EXE001 shebang-exec rules,
  ISC004/SIM115/UP031/SIM117/SIM102 unsafe or unavailable fixes) were reported
  as auto-fixed while `git status` showed no source changes.
- `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` has the same assumption: it counts every
  message and ignores eslint's `output`/`fixed` fields.
- `auto_fix_files()` sets `fixes_applied = len(fixed_findings) > 0`, and the
  human-readable report prints the same findings under both "Auto-fixes
  applied" and "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)" for the same run.
- Existing tests do not assert fix-detection: `tests/test_refactor/
  test_auto_fix.py` mocks entries that include a `fix` payload but never
  asserts the parser checks it, and parser fixtures without a `fix` payload
  are expected to be counted.

## Desired change

- Count a finding as auto-fixed only when the linter actually applied (or
  would apply within safe scope) an edit: ruff `fix` non-null and safe; eslint
  `output`/`fixed` evidence; alternatively verified by comparing file content
  before/after the run.
- Leave unfixed/unsafe diagnostics out of `fixed_findings` so they flow into
  smell detection and are reported under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)"
  only — never duplicated.
- Add the AC 3–4 regression tests, correct existing parser fixtures, and
  update `docs/refactor.md` where the example semantics change.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — `_parse_ruff_fix_output()`, `_parse_eslint_fix_output()`, `auto_fix_files()` need real fix-detection (non-null `fix` / safe applicability / before-after diff).
- `tests/test_refactor/test_auto_fix.py` — existing parser tests must assert fix-detection; add non-fixable → `Auto-fixed: 0` and safe-fix → file-changed regression tests.
- `docs/refactor.md` — § Auto-Fix semantics (`auto_fix.fixed_findings` / `fixes_applied`) updated to state only actually-applied fixes are counted.

## Related work

- SA-0MVRMXK5C005IXQP — duplicate discovery from the 2026-10-28 full-scan run
  ("refactor skill reports false auto-fixes for unfixable linter
  diagnostics"); its richer spec (expected behaviour, `fix.applicability`
  detail, eslint `output`/`fixed` note, linkage to per-diagnostic REFACTOR
  items) is absorbed into this brief; to be closed as a duplicate of this
  item.
- SA-0MQFWFRMQ007CE7H — original "Implement auto-fix for session-introduced

## Goal

As the operator reading my daily standup, I want the "Yesterday I completed work on..." section to separate **auto-dispatched** work (the herdr downtime dispatcher ran `/skill:implement`, `/skill:plan`, `/skill:intake`, `/skill:audit`, `/skill:effort-and-risk` without me) from **manually dispatched** work (I asked an agent to do it in a session I started), so I can see how much of yesterday's progress was machine-driven versus operator-driven.

## Current behaviour

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (`generate_report`, ~line 852) builds `yesterday_items` from `fetch_all_completions_in_window(window_start, window_end)` — every `completed`/`in_review` item whose `updatedAt` falls in the 24 h window, in one flat list.
- Both the markdown report and `yesterday_tts` render that flat list; `--json` exposes a single `yesterday` array.
- Nothing in the pipeline distinguishes provenance, so a `wl next`-selected item implemented by the downtime worker looks identical to one I personally kicked off.

## Provenance signal (already exists — do not invent a new one)

The herdr downtime worker already records provenance in two places:

1. **`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`** — bounded JSONL (cap `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`). Each dispatch entry carries `itemId`, `kind` (`intake`|`plan`|`implement`|`audit`|`risk-effort`|`scheduled`), `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`, `stage`, and post-spawn enrichment fields (`paneId`, `outcome`). `downtime-coordination.log` and `local-route.log` are separate files and must NOT be treated as dispatch markers.
2. **Worklog comment marker** — `buildDowntimeDispatchComment()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, ~line 7951) writes: `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at <ISO> — running <skill> <itemId> (<title>).` This survives the rolling-log trim.

Classification rule to implement: an item is **auto-dispatched** iff it has a matching live dispatch-log entry (`itemId`, and `outcome` is not `spawn-failed`) **or** a worklog comment containing the `Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker at` prefix within/before the window; otherwise **manual**. Items with no detectable marker default to manual (fail-open to the smaller, less confusing bucket) and the default must be documented.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The markdown "Yesterday I completed work on..." section is split into two labelled sub-groups, auto-dispatched first then manual (or an explicitly documented order), each with a plain-language heading (TTS-friendly, e.g. "Work auto-dispatched by the downtime worker" and "Work I dispatched myself").

- [ ] AC2: Each sub-group is omitted when empty; the section never renders an empty heading. If the entire window is empty, the existing empty-section behaviour is preserved.

- [ ] AC3: `--json` exposes the split without breaking the existing contract: `yesterday_auto`, `yesterday_manual` (+ `_count` fields) are added and the existing `yesterday` / `yesterday_count` / `yesterday_tts` keys keep their current meaning (all items, unchanged ordering) so downstream consumers do not regress.

- [ ] AC4: TTS output (`yesterday_tts` renders) speaks the split in first person, e.g. "Yesterday the downtime worker completed..." / "I completed..."; no IDs, backticks, or ISO timestamps in spoken lines.

- [ ] AC5: Classification is unit-tested with fixtures — (a) item with a dispatch-log entry → auto, (b) item with only a worklog comment marker → auto, (c) `outcome: spawn-failed` entry → manual, (d) item with no marker → manual, (e) item in `downtime-coordination.log` / `local-route.log` only → manual, (f) trimmed/absent log file → falls back to comment markers and never raises.

- [ ] AC6: Read-side failures (missing/unreadable `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, unparseable JSONL lines, `wl comment list` failure) degrade gracefully: the report still renders, the affected items land in the manual bucket, and a warning is logged — the exit code stays 0.

- [ ] AC7: `skill/standup/SKILL.md` documents the new section layout, the provenance rule, the default-to-manual behaviour, and the new `--json` fields.

- [ ] AC8: Existing standup tests (`skill/standup/tests/`) remain green; new tests are hermetic (`--no-sync --no-commit`, tmp worklog dirs, no real `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` reads).

## Out of scope

- Counting/dashboards of auto vs manual ratios (follow-up if wanted).
- Changing how the downtime dispatcher records markers.
- Re-ranking or filtering the Herdr selection list (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 rule stands: the Herdr list stays the sole ranking path; the split is presentational grouping only).

## Risks / notes

- The dispatch log is a **rolling 100-entry** log, so a busy day can trim entries within the 24 h window; the comment marker path is the durable fallback and both must be combined by OR.
- `kind: scheduled` entries are dispatcher-driven (scheduled prompts) and should be counted as auto-dispatch; document the decision.
- Grouping must not change item ordering inside a group (keep `updatedAt` then `id` sort) or `yesterday_count`.

Discovered during: `/skill:standup` run on 2026-10-25 for project Worklog.

# Framework pre-push hook v3 should resolve the global test runner

**Origin:** `discovered-from:OSL-0MVMCP5DT005PIFS` (filed from ContentCreator; that item was deleted once this one existed and was synced).

**Headline:** The framework's v3 pre-push hook refuses every `dev`/`main` push unless the pushed repo ships its own `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, so `install_pi.sh` still ships a gate-less v2 hook to every project without one. Make v3 resolve the runner local-then-global (the pattern the same file already uses for the context-budget gate), ship v3 everywhere, and upgrade stale installed copies.

## Problem statement

Only the SorraAgents checkout contains `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`; every other project receives its skills from the global install at `~/.pi/agent/skills`. The v3 hook's full-suite gate looks for the runner at `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` only, so in every non-SorraAgents repo the gate hard-fails (`exit 1`) on any push to `dev`/`main`. `scripts/install_pi.sh` works around that by installing `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — a hook **without** the full-suite gate — into every project that lacks a repo-local runner. The result is two hook variants, and the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee is absent from every project except SorraAgents itself.

The cost is visible: `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` had to hand-write a local-then-global runner lookup into ContentCreator's hook (its only deviation from the framework's) before the full-suite push gate could be restored there.

## Users

- **Agents pushing to `dev`** in any framework project — they need the same push-time guarantee everywhere, not only in SorraAgents.
- **The operator / producer** — one hook to audit, one documented contract, no per-repo fork to drift.
- **Project maintainers running `install_pi.sh`** — a fresh install must not choose a weaker hook, and a stale installed hook must not silently keep the weaker one.

Example user stories:

- As an agent pushing to `dev` in a project with no repo-local `skill/` tree, I want the full suite to run through the global runner, so a red tree is refused before it reaches the shared branch.
- As a maintainer, I want `install_pi.sh` to install one hook for every project, so I never have to reason about which variant my repo received.
- As the operator, I want an incomplete install to refuse the push and name the bypass, rather than silently skipping the gate.

## Desired change

1. **Runner resolution (v3 hook).** Resolve the runner local-then-global inside the full-suite gate, mirroring the context-budget block in the same file:
   - `$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` when present;
   - else `$HOME/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`;
   - when neither exists, fail closed and name `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` (unchanged fail-closed stance, better message).
   This makes the framework hook converge with the block ContentCreator already runs (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` AC2), so the project copy can eventually be deleted rather than forked.
2. **One hook variant.** `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook in every project — the `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` precondition is dropped and `.githooks/pre-push.v2` is removed (or reduced to a pointer note), with the hook-selection comments and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` corrected to describe reality.
3. **Installed-hook upgrade.** `install_pi.sh` must no longer leave a stale installed `.githooks/pre-push` in place forever: when the file's revision marker is a framework revision older than the current one **and the file is an unmodified framework copy**, replace it (backup the previous file, report what happened); when the file carries local modifications, report it and leave it alone. Re-running is idempotent (no rewrite when already current).
4. **Documentation.** The hook contract, the runner resolution order, the revision markers and the upgrade path are documented in the framework docs (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, plus a hook section or `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` mirroring the project-side doc), and the hook header comment states the resolution order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Global runner resolution:** with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` but a global `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, a `refs/heads/dev` push through the v3 hook executes the global runner with `--scope full --strict-git-env` from the pushed repo's root, and a green run permits the push (regression test, fake global runner).
- [ ] **Fail-closed unchanged:** with neither runner present, the hook exits non-zero on a `dev`/`main` push and names `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; feature-branch pushes and `refs/worklog/data` pushes still do not invoke the gate.
- [ ] **Parity with the project hook:** the framework gate block and ContentCreator's `.githooks/pre-push` gate block (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX`) resolve the runner identically — same order, same fail-closed message semantics — asserted by a test that compares the two resolution behaviours (not the whole files, because the Worklog-sync ordering still differs).
- [ ] **One variant shipped:** `install_pi.sh` installs the v3 hook into a project with no repo-local runner (regression test in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`), and no install path can select a hook without the full-suite gate.
- [ ] **Installed-hook upgrade:** an existing `.githooks/pre-push` carrying an older framework revision marker and no local modifications is replaced (with a backup and a report); a locally modified hook is reported and left untouched; a second run changes nothing.
- [ ] **Upgrade safety:** upgrading a project that previously ran the v2 hook preserves its existing gate behaviour (branch policy, context budget, Worklog sync semantics) — the replaced hook is the framework v3 hook verbatim, and a test asserts the installed file's revision marker and gate blocks.
- [ ] **Testing/validation criterion:** full SorraAgents suite passes with the new tests, including `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py`.
- [ ] **Documentation:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, hook header, install script comments; the project-side `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` is referenced, not edited, since it lives in ContentCreator).
- [ ] **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- ✗ Do not weaken the gate: the missing-runner path stays fail-closed, `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` stays the only bypass, `--scope full --strict-git-env` stays mandatory.
- ✗ Do not change branch-policy, context-budget or Worklog-sync semantics as a side effect of the runner fix.
- ✗ Do not overwrite a hook that carries local modifications (ContentCreator's copy deliberately keeps per-push Worklog sync — `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3); detect and report instead (see Q4).
- ✗ Framework code is edited in the SorraAgents repo, never from a project worktree.
- ✗ No ad-hoc test runs during implementation; use the test skill.

## Existing state

- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push` (marker `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`): branch policy → context-budget gate (local-then-global `measure_context.py`) → single stdin capture loop → full-suite gate (`runner="$repo_root/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py"`, hard `exit 1` when absent) → feature-branch early exit → Worklog sync.
- `SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push.v2`: same file without the full-suite gate and without the early exit (Worklog sync runs on every push).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` (~lines 262–310): picks v3 only when `$CURRENT_REPO_ROOT/skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` exists, else copies `pre-push.v2`; copies only when `.githooks/pre-push` is absent, so an installed copy is never refreshed.
- `run_tests.py` resolves the project at CLI time via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so a global invocation is safe as long as cwd is the pushed repo (ContentCreator's hook proves this in production).
- Existing tests: `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` (behavioural, fake local runner), `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` (context-budget local-then-global resolution), `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (v2/v3 selection), `tests/test_context_budget_rollout_docs.py` (doc/hook comment assertions).
- ContentCreator's hook already implements the target resolution and failing-test reporting; it is the reference implementation, differing from framework v3 only in that deviation plus the retained per-push Worklog sync.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/pre-push` — full-suite gate: add local-then-global runner resolution mirroring the context-budget block; improve the missing-runner message; bump the revision marker.
- `.githooks/pre-push.v2` — remove (single-variant install), or convert to a deprecation note if a test depends on its presence.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — drop the runner precondition, always install v3, add the revision-marker upgrade step with backup and local-modification detection, update comments.
- `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py` — add global-runner and neither-runner cases (fake runner injected into a fake `$HOME`).
- `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` — extend the existing fallback harness to the test runner (or add a sibling test module for it).
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — install-into-project-without-runner, upgrade-of-stale-copy, local-modification-preserved, idempotence.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — hook contract and variant documentation corrected; runner resolution and upgrade path added.
- `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (framework) — optional: the framework-side companion to ContentCreator's doc.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (behaviour regression in ContentCreator):** a wholesale overwrite of an existing hook would drop ContentCreator's per-push Worklog sync (framework v3 exits early on feature pushes). Mitigation: overwrite only unmodified framework copies (Q4); report modified ones.
- **Risk (global runner resolves the wrong project):** the global `run_tests.py` resolves its repo from cwd; if the hook ran it from anywhere else, it would test the wrong tree. Mitigation: keep `cd "$repo_root"` (already the case in the project hook) and assert the cwd in the regression test.
- **Risk (install churn):** rewriting hooks on every install produces noisy diffs in every project. Mitigation: revision-marker comparison, no write when current.
- **Risk (scope creep):** ContentCreator's hook fork, the divergent `post-checkout`/`post-merge`/`post-rewrite` hooks, and the release pipeline are out of scope; record as linked items rather than folding them in.
- **Assumption:** this SA item carries the implementation; the `OSL-` origin record was deleted once this item existed and was synced (Q1).
- **Assumption (Q4):** "overwrite existing installed hooks" applies to unmodified framework copies only; locally modified hooks are reported, not clobbered.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` — *Restore the full-suite pre-push gate in ContentCreator* (completed): the project-side fix whose comment filed this follow-up; its Q3 decision (keep per-push Worklog sync) constrains the overwrite.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` — *install_pi.sh propagates the SorraAgents-only test gate to non-SorraAgents projects* (completed): introduced the v2/v3 split this item retires.
- `SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG` — pre-push gate duration vs `implement.py` push timeout (cold-cache cost of the gate).
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full suite deferred from finish to the dev-push gate.
- `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` — finish-gate false green that surfaced the missing push gate.
- `OSL-0MVK2F1Z300996SA` — the item whose `9c88625c` was pushed red.
- `OSL-0MTMS9R58000J613`, `OSL-0MT5Z8AJ7008LCQQ` — earlier pre-push hook defects (non-fatal `wl sync`, author-identity gate).
- `SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK` — active pre-push hook vs committed v3 wiring drift (same hook, adjacent defect).
- `SA-0MVB713300020UFB` — migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (touches the same test fixtures).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (ownership/location).** Where should the implementation and the tracked item live?
  - Options: (a) create a sibling `SA-` item in the SorraAgents store and delete this `OSL-` item as the origin record; (b) implement in SorraAgents but keep this `OSL-` item as the tracked item; (c) keep it ContentCreator-local.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — repository-boundary rule; matches `OSL-0MVKT9LN10097FA2` → `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — "delete this item when the SA item is created and synced". Implementation: sibling `SA-` item created in the SorraAgents store; this `OSL-` item deleted after both stores sync.
- **Q2 (install_pi.sh scope).**
  - Options: (a) full unification — v3 for every project, drop `pre-push.v2`, overwrite existing installed hooks; (b) runner fallback only, leave the variant selection; (c) runner fallback + v3 for new installs, never overwrite, document a manual upgrade.
  - **Recommended:** (c) — overwriting risked clobbering ContentCreator's deliberate deviation.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)** — full unification, including overwriting existing installed hooks. Consequence recorded in Q4.
- **Q3 (missing-runner behaviour).**
  - Options: (a) fail closed naming `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`; (b) fail open with a warning.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — the documented "a red tree is never pushed" guarantee must not vanish silently.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **(a)**.
- **Q4 (derived from Q2 = a; flagged for producer confirmation).** Overwriting installed hooks conflicts with ContentCreator's deliberate deviation: its hook keeps per-push Worklog sync, while framework v3 exits early on feature-branch pushes (`OSL-0MVL2OUW0003C6YX` Q3), and `tests/test_pre_push_hook.py` there asserts sync on feature pushes. Two readings of "overwrite":
  - (i) overwrite unmodified framework copies only (revision marker matches a known framework revision and the file has no local edits); report and skip modified files — **no change to v3's Worklog-sync semantics**;
  - (ii) overwrite unconditionally — requires first changing v3 so feature-branch pushes still sync, i.e. deleting the early exit and updating `tests/test_pre_push_test_gate.py`.
  - **Recommended:** (i) — satisfies Q2 (stale framework copies are upgraded automatically) without changing documented framework hook semantics or breaking another repo's suite. **Status: assumption recorded in this brief; producer to confirm (ii) if unconditional overwrite is wanted.**

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by `find-related` (SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1); full untruncated report at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MVNUMMOA002LCB1.md`.

### Related work items

- **SA-0MUJLT3BH001IPWK** – Reconcile active pre-push hook with committed v3 (context-budget gate wiring drift) (open)
- **SA-0MVB713300020UFB** – Migrate pre-push hook fixtures to `git_sandbox` (blocked) — touches the same hook test fixtures
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed) — unrelated, incidental match

> Repository file matches were generic-word noise (the hook's own tests and
> `audit_runner.py`); the curated **Key Files (predicted)** section is the
> useful list. The two open hook items are genuine neighbours, not duplicates.

# implement.py parent: terminal blockers still gate topological readiness

relocated-from:AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6 (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent` builds its dependency graph from **every** in-chain
dependency edge, including edges whose blocker is already terminal, so a
finished blocker still occupies the topological ordering and delays — or in
practice starves — the genuinely ready child that depends on it. A child whose
blockers are all terminal is *ready now*, yet it can be sorted behind unrelated
children purely because its (finished) blocker had a high `sortIndex`.

## Users

- **Primary — agent/operator running an epic:** "As the agent driving an epic
  with `implement.py parent`, I want a child whose blockers are all already
  finished to be selected as soon as it is the lowest-sorting ready child, so
  in-flight implementation work is never skipped and I never have to finish it
  manually."
- **Secondary — producer/reviewer:** "As a producer, I want the reported
  implementation order to mean 'blockers first, then sortIndex', so I can
  predict which child the next run will start."
- **Maintainer:** "As a maintainer, I want the ordering fix covered by a
  regression test with the exact shape that broke, so the readiness rule
  cannot silently regress."

## Observed failure (2026-10-23, epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S)

Resolved order for the epic's 8 children:

`[TOOK(test-failure, done), 3X5M, MVIS(done), VDA9, 7NGZ, O53Z(done), K0V4, BAAN]`

`K0V4` (sortIndex 3000 — the *lowest* open child) has an outbound `depends-on`
edge to `O53Z` (its test-first contract child, sortIndex 8100). `O53Z` was
already `completed`, so `K0V4` should have been ready immediately; instead it
was released only after `O53Z`'s slot near the end of the queue.

Consequences:

1. `implement.py parent AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S` never reached `K0V4` although its
   worktree held a completed in-flight implementation — it returned
   "start child VDA9"; the in-flight work had to be finished manually with
   `implement.py finish K0V4`.
2. The reported order is not "blockers first" in any intuitive sense: a ready
   child was deferred behind unrelated children purely because its finished
   blocker sorted late.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Terminal blockers never gate readiness.** In
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` an in-chain dependency edge whose blocker
   is terminal — `_is_terminal_child()` is true: status in `TERMINAL_STATUSES`
   (`in_review`, `completed`, `done`, `deleted`) or the item is soft-deleted —
   contributes neither to `in_degree[child]` nor to `dependents[blocker]`. The
   graph is therefore built over non-terminal children only, and a child whose
   in-chain blockers are all terminal is in the **initial** ready set.
2. **Ready children are ordered by their own `(sortIndex, id)`.** For the
   reproduction shape (open child `LOW` with sortIndex 3000 whose only in-chain
   blocker is a `completed` child `HIGH` with sortIndex 8100, plus an unrelated
   open child `MID` with sortIndex 5000) the resolved order starts with `LOW`,
   then `MID`, then `HIGH` — i.e. `LOW`'s position is decided by its own
   `sortIndex`, never by its blocker's.
3. **Regression test reproduces the exact shape.** A new
   `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` covers at
   minimum: (a) the reproduction shape above, asserting `LOW` is **first**;
   (b) an all-terminal children set, asserting ordering is purely
   `(sortIndex, id)`; (c) a non-terminal chain `A ← B` (both open), asserting
   `A` precedes `B` (real blocking still respected); (d) a soft-deleted blocker
   treated as terminal; (e) an external blocker (id not among the children)
   creating no edge; (f) the existing cycle path still returning
   `([], error)` with the cyclic children named; (g) `_next_child_to_implement`
   still refusing a child whose in-chain blocker is **non**-terminal. The
   reproduction test must be shown red against the pre-fix source and green
   after the fix.
4. **No change to adjacent behaviour.** Cycle detection (fail-fast, no infinite
   recursion), cross-project/external-blocker reporting, `_classify_child`
   (`skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress`) and the blocked-child guard in
   `_next_child_to_implement` are unchanged, and the parent still advances once
   every child is terminal.
5. **Documentation updated.** The
   `_resolve_implementation_order()` docstring states the readiness rule
   (terminal blockers are pre-satisfied), and the parent-recursion/dependency
   ordering text in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (plus any `docs/dev/*` reference
   that describes the ordering) is updated to match; code comments explain why
   terminal edges are excluded.
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** — the
   implement-skill group (`pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`) is green and the
   full suite (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full`) passes on the
   committed tip.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code is agent infrastructure owned by **SorraAgents**:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout contains no `skill/` tree). The item
  was relocated here from the AI_Hell worklog (AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6) by producer
  decision, following the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent, while keeping its
  `discovered-from` link to the AI_Hell epic that exposed the defect. The change,
  its tests, docs, commit and full-suite evidence therefore all stay inside this
  repo — `implement.py start <id>` from this checkout creates the worktree here
  and `wl` resolves this store, so no cross-store resolution is involved.
- **Explicit authorisation to edit `skill/`.** The repository-boundary rule
  forbids editing `skill/` unless explicitly instructed; this work item *is*
  that instruction, scoped to the files listed under **Key Files**.
- **Determinism preserved.** Tie-break stays `(sortIndex, id)`; no
  non-deterministic iteration order (sets are always sorted before use).
- **Narrow scope.** Do **not** change `wl dep` semantics, `sortIndex`
  generation/assignment, child classification, or the `parent` phase's broader
  control flow.
- **No new runtime dependencies;** Python 3.8+ compatible; stdlib only (as the
  existing module is).

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`:

- `TERMINAL_STATUSES = {"in_review", "completed", "done", "deleted"}` (~line
  769), `_is_terminal_status()` (~772), `_is_terminal_child()` (~784, also
  treats a soft-deleted `deletedBy` child as terminal).
- `_classify_child()` (~810) — `skip-terminal` / `skip-in-progress` /
  `implement`.
- `_resolve_implementation_order(children, blockers)` (~836) — Kahn's
  algorithm; today:

  ```python
  for edge in blockers.get(cid, []):
      bid = str(edge.get("id", ""))
      if bid in child_ids:              # <-- terminal blockers still counted
          in_degree[cid] += 1
          dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  The ready queue is `sorted(... in_degree[cid] == 0 ..., key=(sortIndex, id))`
  and is re-sorted after each release, so a terminal blocker with a high
  `sortIndex` delays its dependent.
- `_next_child_to_implement(children, blockers_map)` (~905) already gates on
  *non-terminal* in-chain blockers (`all(bid in terminal_ids ...)`), so the
  guard and the sort currently disagree — the inconsistency this item fixes.
- Caller `phase_parent` (~5124) calls `_resolve_implementation_order()` and
  returns early on a cycle error; `_next_child_to_implement()` then picks from
  the ordered list.
- Tests live in `skill/implement/tests/` (6 files, `.pi/test-config.json` group
  `implement` → `pytest -q skill/implement/tests/`); **no test currently covers
  `_resolve_implementation_order` or `_next_child_to_implement` directly.**

## Desired change

- Skip terminal blockers when building the graph in
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` — e.g.

  ```python
  if bid in child_ids and not _is_terminal_child(child_by_id[bid]):
      in_degree[cid] += 1
      dependents[bid].append(cid)
  ```

  (equivalently: collapse terminal children out of the graph before the sort).
  Terminal children remain present in the returned order so the caller still
  reports/finishes them, and their own placement is still decided by their own
  `(sortIndex, id)`.
- Cycle detection then operates over the non-terminal subgraph only; keep the
  same error message/format and the fail-fast return.
- Update the docstring (readiness rule + why terminal edges are excluded) and
  the ordering documentation in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`.
- Add the regression test module described in AC3.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**:
  `_resolve_implementation_order()` graph construction + docstring;
  `_next_child_to_implement()` docstring cross-reference if needed.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_resolve_implementation_order.py` (SorraAgents) —
  **New**: ordering/readiness regression tests (AC3), including the red-then-
  green reproduction shape.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (SorraAgents) — **Edit**: parent-recursion /
  dependency-order text states that terminal blockers do not gate readiness.
- `docs/dev/*` in SorraAgents — **Edit (if present)**: any ordering description
  that contradicts the new rule (verify with
  `grep -rn "topological\|dependency order" docs/ skill/implement/`).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- *Masking a real cycle.* Excluding terminal blockers from the graph could hide
  a cycle that passes through a terminal child. Mitigation: a cycle can only
  block work that still needs doing, so detection over the non-terminal
  subgraph is the correct semantics; document it in the docstring and cover it
  with AC3(f) (cycle among non-terminal children still fails fast).
- *Accidental behaviour drift elsewhere.* `_next_child_to_implement()` has its
  own terminal-aware guard; the fix must align with it rather than replace it.
  Mitigation: AC3(g) asserts the guard still refuses non-terminal-blocked
  children; AC4 forbids changing adjacent paths.
- *Cross-repo verification gap.* The AI_Hell audit/CI cannot see SorraAgents
  files, so a green AI_Hell report does not prove the fix. Mitigation: run the
  implement-skill pytest group and the SorraAgents full suite from the
  SorraAgents worktree and record the evidence (red/green, commit hash) on this
  item, per AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- *Test-gate selection.* Changed-scope selection may not see the new test file
  until it is tracked; Mitigation: `git add` before the gate run and confirm the
  `implement` group is selected (otherwise fall back to full scope).
- *Scope creep.* The 2026-10-23 report also notes the confusing reported order
  generally and the manual `finish K0V4` step; richer ordering diagnostics or
  `parent`-phase rework are **not** in scope. Mitigation: record follow-ups as
  separate items (see Related work) rather than widening this fix.

**Assumptions**

- The item now lives in the **SorraAgents** worklog (relocated from AI_Hell by
  producer decision, per the SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 precedent); the AI_Hell epic
  AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S remains recorded as the origin via `discovered-from`.
- Terminal blockers are pre-satisfied for *ordering* purposes but are still
  reported in the resolved order (existing `skip-terminal` classification
  handles them in the loop), so no caller contract changes.
- Soft-deleted children behave as terminal for this rule (they can never be
  implemented) — consistent with `_is_terminal_child()`.

## Related work

Cross-repo (SorraAgents — the code's owning repo; automated `find-related`
searched only the AI_Hell store because the item's prefix pins that store, and
its file matches are noise here):

- **SA-0MSQIJBTB008RHS1** — *completed* — V2: Dependency-graph resolution,
  topological ordering & cycle detection; the change that introduced
  `_resolve_implementation_order()`.
- **SA-0MSQBM2FK005NW1T** — *completed* — implement skill: `/skill:implement
  <parent-id>` must automatically implement children and blockers in the chain;
  defined the in-chain/external blocker split and the blocked-child guard.
- **SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876** — *open* — implement.py parent ignores the
  do-not-delegate tag when selecting the next child; same selection path
  (`_next_child_to_implement`), different rule. **Relocated** from the AI_Hell
  worklog because `implement.py` is SorraAgents-owned — the precedent for the
  OPEN QUESTION below.
- **SA-0MUWNHKQH0034DW9** — *completed* — implement skill: drive all epic
  children to completion (fresh session per child); the `parent`/`drive` flow
  that consumes this ordering.

AI_Hell (origin store — historical, retained for traceability after the relocation):

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** — Create an improved Phase Shift effect — the epic
  whose run exposed the defect (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** — ship skill kebab-case fix — *completed* — the
  cross-repo precedent: AI_Hell item, SorraAgents commit, cross-repo evidence
  recorded on the item.
- **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ** — run-release Discord notification wiring — the
  earlier cross-repo precedent referenced by the above.
- **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81** — implement.py: behind-only child worktree
  mis-detected as "has changes" and auto-finished — *open* — sibling defect in
  the same `parent`/`finish` machinery (no fix overlap).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was held: the seed context (problem statement,
observed impact, expected behaviour, suggested fix and ACs) was sufficient to
draft an actionable brief, and the repo research below answered the remaining
implementation questions.

- **Q1 — Which repository owns the code, and where does the fix land?**
  — Answer (repo research + precedent, not a producer question):
  **SorraAgents**. `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `SorraAgents/skill`; the AI_Hell checkout has no `skill/` tree
  (`find / -name implement.py` → `SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`,
  identical to the installed copy, `diff` clean). Precedent
  **AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB** (AI_Hell item, commit `4be04fa7a` on SorraAgents
  `dev`, cross-repo evidence in a comment) and **AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ**. Source:
  `git log --grep="AH-"` in SorraAgents; comment on AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB.
- **Q2 — Does `implement.py` work at all against a foreign worklog store?**
  — Answer (repo research): yes. `implement.py` routes every `wl` call through
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()`, whose
  prefix-to-sibling scan maps an `AH-…` id to `AI_Hell/.worklog` even when cwd
  is SorraAgents, so `implement.py start AH-0MVL5B7C80000MT6` from the SorraAgents
  checkout yields a SorraAgents worktree + AI_Hell worklog. Source:
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (~lines 290–370).
- **Q3 — How should terminal be defined for the readiness rule?**
  — Answer (repo research): reuse `_is_terminal_child()` (statuses
  `in_review`/`completed`/`done`/`deleted` plus soft-deleted), matching the
  guard already used by `_next_child_to_implement()`. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (~769–808, ~905–955).
- **Q4 — Is there an existing test to extend?**
  — Answer (repo research): no. `skill/implement/tests/` has 6 modules and none
  imports `_resolve_implementation_order` / `_next_child_to_implement`
  (`grep -rn` clean), so AC3 creates a new module covered by the existing
  `.pi/test-config.json` `implement` group. Source: repo inspection.
- **Q5 — Should this item be relocated to the SorraAgents worklog?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **yes — recreate it on
  `../SorraAgents`, `wl sync`, and delete the AI_Hell item when done.**
  Rationale/precedent: `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by
  SorraAgents (SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 was relocated for the same reason), so all
  such items now live in the owning repo; the cross-repo pattern of
  AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB (AI_Hell item, SorraAgents commit, cross-repo evidence
  comment) is superseded for future items. Research: two conflicting precedents
  were found (AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB kept the item in AI_Hell; SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876
  relocated) — the producer resolved in favour of relocation. Source:
  interactive reply + the `relocated-from` note in SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876.
## Related work (automated report)

# Add a "In This Release" heading to Discord release notification

## Problem statement

The Discord release notification sent by the ship skill embeds an overview
block (project pitch, release focus, project/version line, optional CTA)
directly followed by the changelog (the summary of changes in this release),
with no visual separator. Readers cannot tell at a glance where the "what the
game is" description ends and the "what changed" list begins.

## Users

- Project operators and Discord community members who read the ship skill's
  post-release notification.

### Example user story

> As a Discord member reading a release announcement, I want a clear
> "In This Release" heading before the change list, so I can immediately spot
> what is new without scanning past the overview paragraphs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `buildDiscordPayload` emits a `## In This Release` markdown heading as its
  own paragraph immediately before the changelog paragraph in the embed
  description (real changelog body or the "No changelog available" fallback).
- The existing paragraph order is preserved: pitch → focus →
  `**<projectName> v<version>**` line → CTA → `## In This Release` → changelog.
- The fully-composed description still respects the ≤ 4096 char Discord limit
  with the ellipsis marker (heading included in the truncation).
- Unit tests in `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` cover the heading
  placement (including with/without pitch/CTA) and the truncation boundary.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Discord readers of release notifications can now immediately distinguish the
game overview from the list of changes thanks to a clear "In This Release"
heading.

## Constraints

- Markdown heading embedded in the Discord embed description (markdown is
  rendered by Discord).
- Behaviour stays non-blocking — a notification failure must never change the
  release exit code.
- Heading text `## In This Release` (as specified in the work item; treated as
  flexible but this exact wording is the default).

## Existing state

`buildDiscordPayload()` in `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` composes the
embed description as paragraphs joined with `

` in this order (composition
AC5): (a) project elevator pitch, (b) release focus, (c)
`**<projectName> v<version>**` line, (d) configured CTA, (e) changelog body.
Absent paragraphs are omitted; the result is truncated to ≤ 4096 chars.

## Desired change

Insert a `## In This Release` heading paragraph between the intro block and
the changelog paragraph, i.e. immediately before the changelog body in the
paragraph array, so the heading separates the overview from the change list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Placement assumption:** the heading goes immediately before the changelog
  paragraph. If the operator intended it earlier (e.g. directly after the
  pitch), the change is trivial to adjust — flagged here rather than assumed
  silently.
- **Docs drift:** SKILL.md and both reference docs
  (`skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the top-level
  `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`) currently state the CTA "sits
  immediately before the changelog"; after this change the heading does —
  the docs must be updated in the same change (already a Key File).
- **Scope creep:** no reordering of existing paragraphs or heading-tool changes
  (e.g. dynamic per-release headings) is in scope; record such ideas as
  separate work items, not here.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — `buildDiscordPayload()` adds the
  `## In This Release` heading paragraph before the changelog paragraph.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — extend `buildDiscordPayload`
  tests (and the CTA-composition block) to assert heading placement.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — description-composition bullet updated to mention
  the heading.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — composition documentation
  updated to mention the heading.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — the top-level ship implementation
  reference likewise documents the embed description composition (paragraph
  order and CTA placement) and must be updated to mention the heading.

## Related work

_Duplicate check performed: `wl search` for discord/release/notification
found the original capability (SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z) and the composition work
(SA-0MUU45U8Q008MKGK, SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K, SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD) — none add
an "In This Release" heading; no overlapping completed item found._

- SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z — Ship skill: send Discord message with release details
  + changelog (original Discord notification capability; completed).
- SA-0MUU45U8Q008MKGK — Discord release report: add project elevator pitch and
  per-release focus paragraphs (established the paragraph composition;
  completed).
- SA-0MUWCIFU2006K39K — Add CTA to release report (introduced the CTA
  paragraph that "sits immediately before the changelog"; completed).
- SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD — Ship report to discord needs titling (embed titling;
  completed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview was required: the seed description ("a heading, such as
  '## In This Release' between the two paras") together with the existing
  composition code fully determines the change. Placement assumption
  (answered by Map, agent — based on the work-item description and the
  existing `buildDiscordPayload` composition order): the heading is inserted
  immediately before the changelog paragraph, preserving all other paragraph
  order; the "No changelog available" fallback keeps the heading too, since
  that paragraph still represents the "changes in this release" slot.
  Source: `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` (buildDiscordPayload) and
  work-item description SA-0MVPXI0J9006IZ14.
data.title: Add a "in this release" heading to discord release notification

# plan-if-needed overwrites operator-confirmed effort/risk

Discovered-from: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 (plan session 2026-10-27).

## Problem

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` `plan-if-needed` re-runs the effort-and-risk
estimator whenever no prior `effort_and_risk_skill` comment exists on the item
(`is_effort_risk_computed`), silently overwriting operator-confirmed
effort/risk values with heuristic estimates. On SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 the
operator-confirmed carry-over risk High / effort M was replaced with Extra
Small / Low (comment 09:38:39Z), materially understating risk of a commit-gate
change. The original values were restored manually.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-if-needed` never overwrites an explicitly set/human-confirmed
      effort or risk with a heuristic recomputation; the recompute path is gated
      on the absence of a deliberate value (with a recorded rationale), or the
      overwrite is surfaced as an explicit warning/approval.
- [ ] A regression test covers the overwrite scenario (operator value present,
      no prior estimator comment) and asserts the value is preserved.
- [ ] Origin case documented: SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2 restore comment
      SA-C0MVQKM7XD0089OVQ.

## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).

## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.
data.title: Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime

## Goal

**As** a project owner scaffolding agent guidance from this repository, **I want** `templates/project-AGENTS.md` to carry the project-level conventions that audits actually enforce, **so that** a new project inherits the two rules that a 2026-10-29 cross-project audit session had to invent on the spot instead of discovering them late.

Discovered-from: `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V` (ContextHub) — an epic audit that returned `Ready to close: No` on an acceptance criterion the producer had already decided to accept, and an `implement` run whose push gate did not run the suite the skill documentation says it runs.

## Scope note (read before implementing)

The definite "the template" is taken to mean **`templates/project-AGENTS.md`** — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed consumed by `scripts/init_project_agents.py` (see `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md`). That file is deliberately minimal ("reference structure only"), so this item **adds project-level guidance sections, not a copy of the global rules**.

If the intent was instead the framework sources (`skill/audit`, `skill/report`, `skill/implement`) rather than the project template, re-scope this item before implementing — the framework findings are listed at the end as separate, unfiled work.

## Problem

Two conventions were needed during the ContextHub epic and neither is documented for a project owner:

1. **Recording a producer-accepted acceptance-criteria variance.** The producer decided to accept one AC without the last piece of live evidence. The audit runner ignores `wl auditWaiver` entirely (`grep -n waiver skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → no matches); the *only* way to make an audit score that criterion `adjusted` (non-blocking) instead of `partial` (blocking) is to write the accepted variance into the criterion's own text in the work-item description, resolve the recorded open question, and *additionally* record `wl audit-waive` so the closure guard and `wl doctor audit-gaps` agree. Done that way, the epic audit returned `Ready to close: Yes` with the criterion `adjusted`, a clean Phase 1/Phase 2 (`calls=2 parse_ok=2`). Done any other way it silently stays blocking and the item ping-pongs between implement and audit.
2. **Declaring the project's real push gate.** `skill/implement` and `skill/audit` both state that the dev-push pre-push hook enforces the full suite (`run_tests.py --scope full`). That is true only where the v3 hook is installed: this repository ships `.githooks/pre-push` (v3, with the scope-aware test gate), but a project seeded earlier (ContextHub) still runs `worklog:pre-push-hook:v2`, which enforces branch policy, the context budget and worklog sync **and nothing else**. Green test evidence therefore came from the `implement.py finish` full-scope run, not the hook. A project owner needs to be told to assert this, because the failure mode is silent: pushes succeed and the cached full-suite evidence the audit consumes read-only never exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `templates/project-AGENTS.md` gains a `## Recording an accepted acceptance-criteria variance` section stating the three-step procedure — (a) amend the criterion's text in the work-item description with an explicit "Accepted variance (producer decision, <date>)" clause naming what evidence stands in for the missing evidence, (b) resolve the corresponding open question in the item description, (c) record `wl audit-waive <id> --reason "<why>"` — and explains **why** the description is mandatory (the audit runner scores an AC from its text and ignores `auditWaiver`).
- AC2: The same template gains a `## Declaring your push gate` section telling a project owner to verify which pre-push hook version the project actually runs (`git config core.hooksPath` + the `worklog:pre-push-hook:vN` banner line) and to record the answer in the project's own guidance, so the full-suite evidence an audit consumes is known to exist (or is known to come from `implement.py finish` instead of the hook).
- AC3: `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` is updated to match — it must describe the template as carrying these two optional guidance sections and stay truthful about the "reference structure only, never a copy of the global rules" constraint; `scripts/init_project_agents.py` output must remain idempotent (re-running never duplicates the reference or the new sections).
- AC4: A test pins the guarantee: emitting a fresh project `AGENTS.md` via `scripts/init_project_agents.py` produces a file containing both new sections, and re-running it is a no-op (`scripts/init_project_agents.py --dry-run --json` reports no change).
- AC5: The two conventions stay project-scoped: no global workflow rule is duplicated into the template (the global layer remains `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), and `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is re-measured only if the template changes the always-loaded surface.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced by the dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `templates/project-AGENTS.md` — the canonical project `AGENTS.md` seed; the two new sections go here.
- `scripts/init_project_agents.py` — the installer that reads the template (`TEMPLATE_PATH`) and must stay idempotent.
- `docs/dev/project-agents-md.md` — the installer documentation to keep in sync (it quotes the canonical file verbatim, so the quoted block must be updated too).
- `tests/` — wherever the installer's tests live (`grep -rln "init_project_agents" tests/`), for the AC4 pin.

## Constraints

- Do **not** copy global agent rules (workflow, wl lifecycle, coding disciplines) into the template — that duplication was removed by `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` and must not come back.
- Project-specific guidance stays project-specific: both new sections are conventions a *project owner* opts into, not new global mandates.
- Keep the installer idempotent and its output deterministic; no new dependency.
- UK English; match the existing Markdown style of the file and its quoted copy in the docs.

## Related findings from the same session (not in this item's scope — file separately if wanted)

1. `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` maps an AC verdict of `adjusted` to `unmet` in its Acceptance Criteria table (it only knows `met`/`unmet`), so a *passing* audit that carries an accepted variance renders as `❌ failed` with an `unmet` row. The report had to be corrected by hand.
2. `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py start` fails (`ERROR: Failed to create worktree …`) when a feature branch with the expected name still exists but its worktree directory was removed; the operator has to `git worktree add <path> <branch>` manually and re-run `start` (which then resumes idempotently).
3. `skill/audit` in-main-slot mode (default) emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` child screens that, when unserviced, produce a `Ready to close: No` whose AC rows are all `partial` **and** persist partial child audits that later block the parent — `--no-child-in-main-slot` was the only path that produced a usable report in three consecutive runs.
