# Stop ship invalidating unchanged audits

## Summary

Implement the RCA-directed minimal change so a ship run no longer leaves content-unchanged (v2-verified) audits reading as out of date after the close/re-stage writes — without re-running the audit pipeline for the backlog, without weakening verdict semantics, and without regressing the SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL stale-audit false-block fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Implements the minimal change so that a ship run does not leave content-unchanged audits reading as out of date — preserving the audit freshness signal through the close/re-stage write (e.g. a truthful content fingerprint of the final description) — **without** re-running the expensive audit pipeline for the backlog and without weakening verdict semantics.
- The content-fresh fast path (`hasContentFingerprint` / `queryContentFreshness` / `attemptAuditRemediation`) and the child-reuse gate are preserved; `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- No mass re-audit: the audit pipeline is not fanned across the in-review/backlog set; read-only probes stay read-only (no test-suite execution or pi calls from the freshness probe).
- Legacy/manual audits (no v2 line) resolve per the RCA decision: either the smallest truthful mechanism (applied only when content-unchanged can be verified) or the documented intended side effect, with any display-only consumer (herdr, separate repository) filed as a linked item rather than edited here.
- Any freshness metadata written at close is truthful (fingerprint of the final description; original `auditedAt` and verdict preserved) — never fabricated.
- The stale-audit false-block regression tests (SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL) and the F2 freshness tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the RCA-recommended change: content-aware classification in `planAuditRefresh` / the stale-flag consumers and/or a truthful close-path freshness-signal preservation in the `run-release.js` close/cascade/comment writes (or the runner's persistence helpers).
- Keep every probe read-only and bounded; introduce no lifecycle `wl` writes beyond the existing close path.

# Intake Brief: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

## Problem statement

When a release re-audits work items (gate remediation, freshness re-runs), the
items are sometimes re-armed with `needsProducerReview`, so the producer is
asked to re-approve work the release itself has just touched. The desired rule
is simple: **require a producer review only when the audit failed for any
reason, or when code/content changed since the last review** — never because a
passing re-audit of unchanged work ran during a release.

## Users

- **Producer (operator)** — user story: "When I run a release I don't want the
  release's own re-audits to put passing, unchanged items back into my review
  queue; I only want to see genuine failures or actual changes."
- **Release engineer / automated release agent** — user story: "I want the
  producer-review flag to mean exactly 'the producer must look now', so the
  release gate neither blocks on already-reviewed unchanged work nor silently
  lets a failed item drop off the queue."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Producer-review policy is stated and enforced.** `needsProducerReview` is
   set only when (a) the audit failed for any reason (an independent or
   ship-triggered verdict of `Ready to close: No`), or (b) the item's audited
   content/code changed since the last producer review. A passing re-audit of
   unchanged work — including during a release — never sets it.
2. **Failed ship-triggered re-audits still surface to the producer.** A
   ship-gate re-audit (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned `--ship-triggered` path)
   whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still sets `needsProducerReview` for
   the item to reach the producer queue; the ship-triggered carve-out
   suppresses only the passing/verification case. Where this diverges from
   SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ AC1 ('No' verdict leaves the flag untouched), the
   producer's stated rule in this item takes precedence and the divergence is
   reconciled (that item's Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer
   confirmation, which this item provides).
3. **Code/content-change trigger is not swallowed.** The ship-triggered
   suppression never overrides the content-fingerprint change signal: a
   ship-triggered re-audit of an item whose audited content changed since the
   last review still resolves to `required`, exactly as an independent audit
   would.
4. **Targeted tests.** Tests exercise production code and lock: passing
   unchanged re-audit → no flag write; failed re-audit (independent and
   ship-triggered) → flag write; content change → flag write; marker absence
   → flag behaviour unchanged.
5. **Documentation updated.** `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and
   `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` document the
   only-when-failed-or-changed flag rule and the ship-triggered carve-out
   boundary (passing suppressed, failing/change still flagged).
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Producers stop being asked to re-review work the release simply re-audited,
while genuine audit failures and real changes still land in their queue.

## Constraints

- **Independent audit behaviour unchanged.** Audits run outside release
  automation keep today's flag rules exactly (SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST,
  SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42, SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H preserve/required/untouched
  semantics); only ship-automated verification runs are touched.
- **No new flag-clearing behaviour.** Suppression means "don't write the
  flag", never `--needs-producer-review no` retro-clearing; the ship close
  step's authorised override (SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q) is unchanged.
- **Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ before/while implementing.** That item
  is already planned (plan_complete); its 'No'-verdict suppression must be
  reconciled with AC2 of this item rather than silently shipping both.
- **Repository boundary.** Changes live in SorraAgents skills (audit, ship)
  and their docs; no herdr/ContextHub change required.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  (~line 2745) resolves `preserved`/`required`/`untouched`;
  `_passing_audit_producer_decision()` (~line 2674) mirrors the passing
  verdict; `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()` (~line 17122) writes
  `--needs-producer-review yes` when `required`. Existing carve-outs: child
  items never flagged; cascade-demotion-suppressed 'No' untouched;
  tracked/accepted medium/low candidate-false-positive chores untouched.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — release-gate re-audit call sites that run
  `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict` (the SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading is planned but not yet implemented).
- Flag-rule precedents: SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST (preserve review across passing
  re-audits, flag independent failures), SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW (flag when
  automated audit says ready to close), SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H (top-level only).

## Desired change

- Confirm the producer-review flag rule as stated in AC1 and enforce it in the
  audit runner and the release flow: passing re-audits of unchanged items never
  set the flag; failing re-audits and content/code changes always do.
- Reconcile with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ: its ship-triggered marker suppression
  covers the passing/verification case only; the failing-verdict case keeps
  flagging (or the divergence is explicitly recorded and producer-approved).

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_producer_review_decision()`
  and `_passing_audit_producer_decision()`: enforce only-when-failed-or-changed;
  ship-triggered marker consultation must not swallow failure/change signals.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`,
  `refresh-audits.js` — reconciliation with SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ marker
  threading (failing-verdict boundary).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document the flag rule and
  the carve-out boundary.
- `skill/audit/tests/` (`test_audit_runner_producer_review.py`,
  `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`) — AC4 coverage.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ** — Ship skill triggered audits should not mark for
  producer review (open, plan_complete): the planned ship-triggered marker
  mechanism this item's rule constrains; reconciliation required (AC2).
- **SA-0MVR9B1UH002BUST** — Audit runner: preserve a producer's review across
  passing re-audits; flag failing audits (completed): defines the
  preserved/required/untouched decision the release rule extends.
- **SA-0MS1WXHVF008AKQW** — Set producerReview flag when automated audit marks
  item as ready to close (completed): the foundational flag-on-yes rule.
- **SA-0MSSVKYEW008PJ9H** — Audit pass should set needsProducerReview only for
  top-level items (completed): child carve-out.
- **SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42** — audit_runner sets needsProducerReview for every
  medium/low CFP chore (completed): CFP carve-out (same suppression spirit).
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — Ship skill: release-ready parent must override or
  absorb needsProducerReview on children (completed): close-step override kept
  out of scope here.
- **SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G** — Ship skill invalidates audits (open): adjacent
  freshness concern, distinct ACs.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
  (Producer-review flag lifecycle ~lines 444–542), `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — contradictory ACs between items.** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's planned
  AC1 suppresses the flag for ship-triggered 'No' verdicts; AC2 of this item
  requires a failing ship-triggered re-audit to flag. Mitigation: this item
  records Blocked-by (SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ) and the reconciliation is made
  explicit before either is implemented; if the producer prefers the
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ behaviour, AC2 is amended via that item's plan, not
  silently.
- **Risk — marker leakage** (from SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ): the ship-triggered
  marker must not be settable in an operator's shell. Mitigation: adopt the
  planned CLI-flag mechanism, never an env var.
- **Assumption — 'code was changed' = content-fingerprint change.** The only
  change signal the runner has today is the title/description content
  fingerprint; a repo/commits-change signal is out of scope (separate work
  item if desired).
- **Scope-creep guard.** Verdict semantics, close-step overrides, and the
  freshness/time-gate concerns of SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G are deliberately out of
  scope; they remain linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (failing ship-triggered re-audit):** Should a ship-gate
  re-audit whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still set
  `needsProducerReview`, or is demotion out of the release queue sufficient (as
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ's plan assumes)? **Recommended (Map, intake): flag it /
  keep AC2 — this item's seed states the producer's rule that a producer review
  is required whenever the audit failed for any reason, and SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ
  Appendix Q2 explicitly awaited producer confirmation on exactly this point;
  this item is that confirmation.** Source: seed context of SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1
  ("We should only require a producer review if the audit failed for any
  reason, or if code was changed"), SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ Appendix Q2. Not
  independently re-confirmed (operator instructed no repeated producer reviews
  during this intake).
- **Assumption ("code was changed"):** "Code was changed" maps to the audit
  runner's existing content-fingerprint change signal (title/description
  content changed since the last review → fresh audit required), which is the
  only change signal the runner currently has; the item records the policy that
  this signal must keep arming the flag including for ship-triggered runs.
  A broader "repo/commits changed" signal would be a separate work item.
- **Assumption (relationship):** SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ (already planned) is the
  implementation vehicle for the passing-verification suppression; this item
  carries the flag-rule policy and the failing/change boundary; the plan stage
  should reconcile the two (this item records Blocked-by SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ).

## Review log

- Completeness review: brief covers problem, users, ACs, constraints, existing
  state, desired change, key files, related work, appendix — no gaps found.
- Capture fidelity review: seed intent ('only require producer review when the
  audit failed for any reason, or if code was changed') preserved in AC1–AC3;
  SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ 'No'-verdict divergence recorded neutrally.
- Related-work & traceability review: all linked items verified against wl;
  typo SA-0MUJLWPB10038ZQ → SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q corrected.
- Risks & assumptions review: added Risks section (contradictory ACs, marker
  leakage, 'code changed' interpretation, scope-creep guard).
- Polish & handoff review: wording tightened; commands are skill-standard.

## Related work (automated report — find-related)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPD8NXCS0091ZF4** – Ralph crashes reading persisted audit when workItem.audit is an object (completed)
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MQ01FDQ5003H09A** – Implementation: update AMPA audit handlers to use wl audit-set (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+14 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+13 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: afterwards, audit, auditing, automatically, back (+13 more)


---

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-16 (plan skill, herdr downtime dispatch)**: Decomposed SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 into 4 children in test-first dependency order:
  1. `SA-0MWJCDH5K002M5H5` — Test: audit_runner only-when-failed-or-changed producer review decision (leaf, no deps)
  2. `SA-0MWJCDQ3S003EY2R` — Implement: audit_runner only-when-failed-or-changed rule (depends on test + sibling marker SA-0MWJ7K962006646G)
  3. `SA-0MWJCDX79003103I` — Implement: ship-gate failing-verdict boundary reconciliation (depends on runner impl + sibling threading SA-0MWJ7KPC00073EMP)
  4. `SA-0MWJCE2KN000FJBV` — Implement: docs for only-when-failed-or-changed rule (depends on both implements)
  - Chosen reconciliation: the ship-triggered carve-out suppresses only the passing/verification case; failing ('Ready to close: No') and content-change verdicts still resolve `required` (AC2/AC3 boundary, per the producer's stated rule recorded in this item's seed — SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ Appendix Q2 confirmation).
  - Parent Blocked-by SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ formalised as a dependency edge (auto-flips parent to `blocked`; auto-reconciles to `open` when the sibling completes).
  - AC coverage review: 100% covered, `proceed` (no auto-closed children needed; traceability ACs restating all six parent ACs added to the relevant children).

## Plan: Appendix (questions & answers)

- Q1 (failing ship-triggered re-audit): Should a ship-gate re-audit whose verdict is `Ready to close: No` still set `needsProducerReview`? **Answer (plan, adopting intake recommendation encoded in AC2): yes** — this item is the producer confirmation SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ Appendix Q2 awaited; the failing-verdict case keeps flagging and the reconciliation is enforced in children 2/3. No new producer review requested (operator instructed no repeated producer reviews during this run).
- Q2 ('code was changed' definition): Mapped to the existing content-fingerprint change signal, per the intake assumption; child 2 requires the marker never to swallow that signal (AC3).
- Q3 (relationship): SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ provides the ship-triggered marker mechanism; this item constrains its decision boundary. Blocked-by recorded as a dependency edge.
data.title: Do not require repeated producer reviews during release

# Extract metric prose into glossary appendix (F1)

Core implementation slice of SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS ("Move the detailed
descriptions of the metrics into an appendix", incl. merged
LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3). Changes `reporting.py::build_report()` so the main body
of `report.md` carries only **data** (tables, section headers, one-sentence
metric reminders) and all detailed metric-description prose moves to a
metric-glossary appendix appended at the end of the document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Every detailed metric-description passage currently embedded in the body
  (AC1 list in the parent: header bullet block; `## Summary by hour`
  availability footnote + 4 state notes; `## Total tokens`
  "Total = prompt (input) + completion (output)…" paragraph; `## Local model
  utilization` `Busy = at least one local slot active…` / `Method: streams are
  paired…` paragraphs; `## Prefill vs decode` "Every figure here is
  slot-seconds…" explanation; `## Engine cross-check` engine-vs-proxy caveat
  paragraphs; plus per-section interpretation notes across all ~30 sections)
  moves to an appendix at the end of the document.
- AC2: Each metrics table in the body is accompanied by at most a one-sentence
  reminder of its metric's definition (a short gloss under the section header
  or next to the table); a reminder exists for every table whose full
  description moved to the appendix.
- AC3: A metric-glossary appendix (`## Appendix: Metric definitions` or
  equivalent) is appended at the end of `report.md` and contains a glossary
  entry for **every metric in the report** (full glossary rule, producer
  Q2=A): the definition, why it matters, how it is calculated, and — for the
  performance/scorecard metrics — levers and trade-offs
  (LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 content). Entries are generated from the same data
  structures that feed each body section (additive key rule — no
  parser/`--json` key changes), so body and glossary stay in sync — every
  scorecard metric's detail entry lives in the appendix, not duplicated in
  the body.
- AC4: The pipeline stays fully deterministic and rule-based (no LLM in the
  report); section order of the body is preserved; only the prose moves.
- AC5: The body keeps its two intended uses: at-a-glance data (tables + one
  sentence glosssary reminders) and detailed breakdown (appendix).
- AC6: The report still renders for every window shape (empty window,
  zero-traffic, no llama-server logs, GPU data absent) without errors — the
  appendix must not fail on missing data (empty sections render a named
  reason or a data-gated note, matching existing conventions).
- AC7: Any metric added, removed, or restructured while building the appendix
  is documented in the work-item description or a follow-on item (AC5 of the
  parent); no silent changes.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — `build_report()` and
  the `_append_*` helpers; new `_append_metric_glossary` (or equivalent)
  section builder + one-sentence gloss extraction.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — section-specific tests updated by
  T1 (this item's changes must keep the suite green together with T1).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`, `REFERENCE.md`, `README.md` —
  updated by D1 (this item leaves a note of what changed for D1).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: T1 (section-test rewrite encodes the contract).
- Blocks: D1 (docs), T3 (window-shape regression over the new layout).

## Deliverables

- `reporting.py` change: body data-only, one-sentence reminders, appended
  metric-glossary appendix.
- Report renders correctly for all window shapes (verified by T3).

# Top-of-report performance scorecard (F2)

Implementation slice of SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS for the merged LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3
("Performance metrics in usage report"). Adds a **top-of-report scorecard**
section to `report.md`: a summary table of the validated performance metrics
with **baseline, target, actual, met/unmet** columns, built from the validation
work items' measured figures, with every scorecard metric's detailed entry in
the appendix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The scorecard renders as the **first section** of `report.md` (before
  `## Summary by hour`), one row per validated performance metric with
  Metric | Baseline | Target | Actual | Met/Unmet observation columns.
- AC2: The scorecard is built from measured figures of the validation work
  items — at minimum the contention baseline (LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK,
  `CONTENTION_BASELINE` already in `reporting.py`) plus whatever additional
  completed validation items the implementer selects (e.g. engine cross-check
  LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX, capacity signals LP-0MVU8O4EL005IYP9, residency
  LP-0MVT2QHMU0008F2V, evictions LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S, contention
  LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK) — no fabricated figures.
- AC3: Honest degradation: a metric without a measured baseline/target renders
  an explicit "no baseline yet" note (honest-degradation rule already used by
  the report); the scorecard never guesses.
- AC4: Met/unmet uses configured thresholds (from `proxy/config.yaml` when
  present) or measured baselines; when unset, default thresholds are
  documented in the report section itself.
- AC5: Every scorecard metric has its **detail entry in the appendix** (why
  important, how calculated, levers, trade-offs per LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3
  content) — never duplicated in the body; the glossary entry is the single
  home for that detail, so the top-of-report scorecard section (metrics,
  baseline, target, actual, met/unmet observation) is built from the
  validation work items' measured figures with the appendix carrying the
  per-metric detail.
- AC6: The pipeline stays deterministic/rule-based; no parser/`--json`
  key changes unless explicitly additive (extend
  `summary_to_json`/`--json` round-trip tests if keys are added).
- AC7: The scorecard renders safely for every window shape (empty, zero
  traffic, no llama-server logs, GPU absent) — no section omission/error in
  edge windows (shared with T3).

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — new scorecard
  section appended at the top of `build_report()`.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — CLI entry;
  unchanged unless the scorecard needs config plumbing for
  baseline/target values.
- `proxy/config.yaml` (llm-manager) — optional configured thresholds for
  met/unmet.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — scorecard
  tests from T2 flipped green here.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: T2 (scorecard contract tests).
- Blocks: T3 (window-shape regression), D1 (docs).

## Deliverables

- Scorecard section implementation in `reporting.py`.
- Baseline/target wiring (config or structural defaults with documented
  honest degradation).
data.title: Top-of-report performance scorecard

# Docs, code comments & metric-change log (D1)

Documentation slice of SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS (AC5 + AC7). Updates every piece of
documentation that describes the `proxy-usage-analysis` report structure to
match the new layout (data-only body + one-sentence reminders + metric-glossary
appendix + top-of-report scorecard), and records any metric added/removed/
restructured during the appendix build (AC5).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `SKILL.md` describes the new report structure: scorecard first, body
  data-only with one-sentence metric reminders, `## Appendix: Metric
  definitions` as the single home for detailed metric descriptions. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries for `proxy-usage-analysis` (parent AC7).
- AC2: `REFERENCE.md`'s section-by-section report documentation matches the
  implemented layout (section order, what each section contains, where the
  detailed metric entries live, scorecard description with baseline/target
  sources and honest-degradation rule, appendix coverage rule = every metric).
- AC3: `README.md` and any other skill docs referenced in the repo mention the
  new structure where they describe the report; code comments and module
  docstrings in `reporting.py` and `analyze_proxy_usage.py` no longer describe
  prose that moved (comments that explain *why* a figure is computed stay).
- AC4: The metric-change log: any metric added, removed, or restructured while
  building the appendix is documented in the parent work item (SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS)
  description or a follow-on item — AC5 of the parent is satisfied with a
  written record, not just code.
- AC5: No doc claims a detail lives in the body when it now lives only in the
  appendix, and no doc references a section heading that no longer exists.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` (501 lines; section docs incl.
  engine cross-check, capacity signals, contention measurement).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` (1503 lines; per-section
  reference, output schemas, implementation notes).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/README.md` (58 lines).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — comments/docstrings.
- Parent item SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS — metric-change log record (AC5).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: F1 (appendix + reminders) and F2 (scorecard) — docs must
  describe the implemented layout.

## Deliverables

- Updated SKILL.md / REFERENCE.md / README.md / code comments.
- Written AC5 record of metric changes in the parent item.

# Window-shape render regression suite (T3)

Test-side slice of SA-0MW7QD3CJ00208YS AC6: the restructured `report.md`
(still) renders for **every window shape** without errors, and the existing
per-section regression tests are updated where section content changed. This
item is the full-suite/window-shape gate that runs after F1+F2 land.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A window-shape test matrix renders the full report (via
  `build_report()` and/or the CLI fixtures) for each shape and asserts no
  exception and a non-empty render: (1) empty window (no sessions), (2)
  zero-traffic window (sessions but no local activity / no requests), (3) no
  llama-server logs (speed sections + engine cross-check + contention
  sections get no data), (4) GPU data absent (GPU busy row/scorecard entry
  degraded), (5) mixed typical window (existing fixture baseline).
- AC2: All existing per-section regression tests that pin section content
  (section-order tests, prose assertions, JSON round-trips, CLI text summary)
  are updated to the new layout where content changed; the full project test
  suite passes (`pytest` in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`).
- AC3: The appendix and scorecard render data-gated notes (not errors) in
  each degraded shape — this is T3's own assertion, complementary to T1/T2
  contract tests.
- AC4: Tests remain deterministic and rule-based; no test depends on wall
  time or the hourly `datetime.now()` header beyond what existing tests
  already tolerate.
- AC5: No regression in the `--json` machine-readable summary keys (additive
  only) — the existing JSON round-trip tests still pass unchanged or with
  documented additive keys only.

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/` — entire suite; window-shape matrix
  lives in `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` near the other render tests; section
  tests updated per AC2.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — output exercised
  (read-only from this item's perspective).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: F1 (appendix + reminders) and F2 (scorecard) — the matrix must
  exercise the final layout.

## Deliverables

- Window-shape render matrix (5 shapes) + updated per-section regression
  tests; full suite green on llm-manager `dev` (via the dev-push gate).

## Goal

Write the targeted tests for SA-0MWJ8WGQD0073MG1 AC4: the producer-review flag rule 'only when the audit failed for any reason, or code/content changed since the last review' — and the ship-triggered carve-out boundary where a passing re-audit of unchanged work never sets the flag, a failing re-audit (independent or ship-triggered) always does, and a content-change signal is never swallowed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests exercise production code (\`_resolve_producer_review_decision\` / \`_passing_audit_producer_decision\` in \`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py\`), not re-implementations of it.
- Passing unchanged re-audit (top-level 'Yes', reviewed, same fingerprint) → no \`--needs-producer-review\` write, for both an independent run and a ship-triggered run.
- Failed re-audit (top-level 'No') independent → \`--needs-producer-review yes\` written.

## Summary

When a work item's priority is downgraded from **critical** to a lower level (high, medium, or low) via `wl update <id> --priority`, automatically ensure that none of its direct children have a priority higher than **high**. Any critical child should be downgraded to high.

## Background

Critical-priority children of a non-critical parent are contradictory: if the parent is no longer critical, its subtasks shouldn't be either. Currently, `wl update --priority` silently allows this inconsistency to persist.

## User Stories

- **As a** project manager, **I want** critical children automatically downgraded when I downgrade their parent from critical, **so that** I don't have to manually fix child priorities.
- **As a** developer, **I want** the downgraded children reported in the command output, **so that** I can verify the cascade happened correctly.

## Implementation Approach

1. Add a `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` utility function (or method on `WorklogDatabase`) that:
   - Finds all direct children of `parentId` using `getChildren(parentId)`
   - Filters children with `priority === 'critical'`
   - For each such child, updates priority to `'high'` via `db.update(child.id, { priority: 'high' })`
   - Returns the list of updated children

2. In `src/commands/update.ts`, after updating the parent's priority:
   - If the **old** priority was `'critical'` and the **new** priority is NOT `'critical'` (i.e., downgraded)
   - Call `cascadePriorityDowngrade(normalizedId, priorityCandidate)`
   - Include the list of downgraded children in the JSON output
   - In human-readable mode, print a summary line like: `[Downgraded 2 child(ren) from critical to high]`

3. Add unit tests to `tests/database.test.ts`:
   - Test that critical children of a non-critical parent are unaffected
   - Test that critical children are downgraded to high when parent is downgraded
   - Test that children already at high or below are unaffected
   - Test the edge case: parent downgraded from critical to critical (no-op, no children touched)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a critical work item's priority is updated to anything other than critical, all direct children with `priority === 'critical'` are updated to `priority === 'high'`
- [ ] Children with priority `high`, `medium`, or `low` are NOT modified
- [ ] Non-critical parent priority changes do NOT trigger any child changes
- [ ] JSON output for `wl update <id> --priority` includes a `downgradedChildren` array when children were changed
- [ ] Human-readable output includes a summary of downgraded children
- [ ] Unit tests verify all acceptance criteria
- [ ] Full test suite passes

## Problem statement

The post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite git hooks run `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` on every checkout. When such a hook fires **inside a git worktree** (e.g. the `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*/` worktrees created by the implement skill), the sync creates a destructive "Sync work items and comments" commit **on the worktree's own branch** whose tree contains only `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and deletes every other tracked file — a data-loss event that must then be undone with `git reset`.

## Root cause (confirmed by reproduction)

Git exports `GIT_DIR=<worktree-gitdir>` (and clears it only for the hook's direct children) when it invokes a hook. The `wl sync` process spawned by the hook **inherits `GIT_DIR`**, and every `git` command spawned by `withTempWorktree()` in `src/sync.ts` also inherits it. Because `GIT_DIR` overrides repository discovery, `git -C <temp-worktree> ...` commands no longer operate on the freshly created temp worktree — they operate on the **user's worktree** (its HEAD, index, and refs):

1. `git -C <tmp>/wt ls-files -z` lists the **user's** tracked files (all ~497 project files).
2. `git -C <tmp>/wt rm -r -- <file>` for every file except the JSONL stages deletions **in the user's index**.
3. `git -C <tmp>/wt commit -m "Sync work items and comments"` commits the **user's worktree HEAD** with a tree containing only `.worklog/` — the destructive commit, parent = the user's feature commit.
4. `git -C <tmp>/wt push --no-verify origin HEAD:refs/worklog/data` resolves HEAD to the destructive commit and is **rejected (non-fast-forward)** — the error message the hook swallows ("sync failed or not initialized; continuing").

Secondary effects:

- `git worktree add` fires the post-checkout hook **inside the temp worktree** (PWD = `.../.worklog/tmp-worktree-*/wt`); the nested `wl sync` fails harmlessly ("not initialized") only because the temp worktree is uninitialized.
- The leaked `GIT_DIR` also breaks temp-worktree cleanup: `git worktree remove --force` fails, leaving orphaned `tmp-worktree-*` directories behind (observed: `.worklog/tmp-worktree-iSDnEC/wt`, `.worklog/tmp-worktree-lgpVH1/wt`).

The main checkout is unaffected in practice: there `hasRemote=true` means no `git rm -r` path is taken, and sync history on `dev` is clean except for the July-12 incident (`af3388f` + revert `2478af5`), which was fixed by the pre-push safety guard (WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB).

## Users

- **AI agents using the implement skill** — they work in `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-*/` worktrees; any `git checkout`, `git reset --hard`, or `git checkout -- <file>` in the worktree triggers the destructive commit (verified three times during WL-0MS7MFILJ0079283 / WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4).
- **Developers using git worktrees** with Worklog hooks installed.
- **Producers / maintainers** who must clean up the mess (resets, orphaned commits, leftover temp worktrees).

### Example user stories

- As an agent implementing WL-XXXX in a worktree, I can run `git checkout -- <file>` or `git reset --hard <commit>` without my worktree branch being rewritten with a tree-deleting "Sync work items and comments" commit.
- As a developer, I can push from a worktree without the pre-push or post-checkout hooks touching my working tree or branch.
- As a maintainer, I never find orphaned `tmp-worktree-*` directories or surprise "Sync work items and comments" commits in reflogs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Repro documented** — a minimal repro (worktree with initialized `.worklog` + `git checkout -b X`) produces the destructive commit; the AC below verifies it is gone after the fix.
- [ ] **Hooks skip worktrees** — the post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite (via `worklog-post-pull`) hooks skip sync when `git rev-parse --git-dir != git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (mirroring the pre-push hook from WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0) and when `PWD` matches `*tmp-worktree-*`. Both the committed `.githooks/*` templates AND the generated content in `src/commands/init.ts` and `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` are updated.
- [ ] **No destructive commits** — after the fix, running `git checkout`, `git reset --hard`, or `git merge` inside an initialized worktree never creates a commit on the worktree branch and never stages deletions; the worktree tree stays intact.
- [ ] **Defense in depth in `wl sync`** — `withTempWorktree()` runs git commands with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` cleared (as git itself does for hooks), so even a manual `wl sync` inside a worktree cannot touch the caller's branch. Temp-worktree cleanup (`git worktree remove`) succeeds, leaving no orphaned `tmp-worktree-*` dirs.
- [ ] **Tests** — unit tests cover: (a) canonical hook content for post-checkout / worklog-post-pull contains the worktree skip; (b) `gitPushDataFileToBranch` with `GIT_DIR` set (simulating hook env) makes no commit on the current branch and pushes only to `refs/worklog/data`.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** hook marker/version mismatch — if committed `.githooks/*` and generated content (`init.ts`, `hook-upgrade.ts`) diverge, `wl doctor` may flag or rewrite hooks. Mitigation: update all three together and extend `tests/doctor-hook-upgrade.test.ts`.
- **Risk:** regressing main-checkout sync — the guard must only skip *worktrees*; the main checkout must keep syncing from hooks. Mitigation: the `git-dir != git-common-dir` check is precise; covered by tests.
- **Risk:** scope creep on env sanitization — keep the `GIT_*` hardening scoped to `withTempWorktree()`'s git child processes; do not expand into a general env-cleanup refactor.
- **Assumption:** worktrees are feature-development contexts that never need to sync; the main checkout is the sync owner (consistent with `resolveWorklogDir()` giving worktrees their own `.worklog`).
- **Assumption:** the pre-push worktree guard (WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0) is the correct pattern to replicate.

## Constraints

- The fix must not change behavior in the **main checkout** (sync must still run from hooks there).
- The pre-push hook's existing worktree guard (WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0) is the established precedent — reuse the same guard pattern.
- Worktrees intentionally have their own independent `.worklog` (per `src/worklog-paths.ts`); sync from worktrees is not a supported path — skipping is the correct behavior.
- Must not break the temp-worktree mechanism used by `gitPushDataFileToBranch` for legitimate pushes to `refs/worklog/data`.
- Follow build → test → commit discipline (vitest suite).

## Existing state

- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` run `wl sync --git-branch refs/worklog/data` unconditionally (no worktree detection).
- `.githooks/pre-push` **already** skips worktrees (`git-dir != git-common-dir`) and `*tmp-worktree-*` PWDs — fixed in WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0.
- `src/commands/init.ts` generates the post-checkout hook content (~line 430) and the central `worklog-post-pull` script (~line 360) without worktree detection.
- `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` `generateCanonicalHookContent()` generates post-checkout (line ~133) and worklog-post-pull (line ~190) content without worktree detection; the pre-push case (line ~84) already has it.
- `src/sync.ts` `withTempWorktree()` (line ~752) and `gitPushDataFileToBranch()` (line ~827) spawn git via `contextExec` with the inherited (possibly GIT_DIR-polluted) environment.
- The destructive commits `0509caaa`, `b772812d`, `5bdf6ce1` (Jul 31 session, orphans now) and my repro commits `cf779f70`, `1ce8fdff`, `71ed5ad1`, `bfb7b67a` all show the same shape: parent = worktree HEAD, tree = only `.worklog/`, message "Sync work items and comments".

## Desired change

1. Add the worktree-skip guard (and `*tmp-worktree-*` PWD guard) to `.githooks/post-checkout` and `.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, and to the generated content in `src/commands/init.ts` and `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts`. Bump hook markers if the canonical/installed comparison (`doctor/hook-upgrade.ts`) requires it.
2. Harden `withTempWorktree()` / `gitPushDataFileToBranch()` (or `contextExec`) to run git commands with a sanitized environment (`GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` unset) — the same "unset" git itself performs for hooks. This also fixes temp-worktree cleanup failures.
3. Add regression tests (see ACs).

## Key Files

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — committed hook template; add worktree-skip guard.
- `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — committed central post-pull script (used by post-merge/post-rewrite); add worktree-skip guard.
- `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite` — thin wrappers delegating to `worklog-post-pull`; no change expected beyond the shared script.
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `installPostCheckoutHook` / central post-pull generation (~lines 264–490); must emit the same guards so newly initialized repos are safe.
- `src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` — `generateCanonicalHookContent()` post-checkout (~line 133) and worklog-post-pull (~line 190) cases; must match the committed hooks so `wl doctor` doesn't flag/regress them.
- `src/sync.ts` — `withTempWorktree()` (~line 752) and `gitPushDataFileToBranch()` (~line 827); clear `GIT_*` env for child git processes (defense in depth) and ensure temp-worktree cleanup succeeds.
- `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` — extend with GIT_DIR-leak / hook-env scenario.
- `tests/doctor-hook-upgrade.test.ts` — verify canonical post-checkout / worklog-post-pull content includes the worktree skip.

## Related work

- WL-0MRIEPH3J006RAPL — "wl sync corrupts dev branch when run from git worktree" (completed): the July-12 incident (`af3388f` on `dev`); same destructive-commit shape, fixed by the refs/worklog/ safety guard + `--no-verify` temp-worktree push.
- WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0 — "Make pre-push hook safe in worktree and temp worktree contexts" (completed): established the worktree-skip pattern in `.githooks/pre-push` that this item must replicate for post-checkout/post-pull.
- WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB — original pre-push-corruption bug (guards in `gitPushDataFileToBranch`).
- WL-0MRIFV2OW002DDAN — added `--no-verify` to temp-worktree push (dependency of WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0).
- WL-0MLLG2CD41LLCP0T / WL-0MLTDQ1BU1KZIQVB / WL-0ML0IFVW00OCWY6F / WL-0MRTSPCNZ001XWRN — worktree init/cleanup/test work (context).
- WL-0MS7MFILJ0079283, WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4 — the herdr panes work in whose worktrees the bug was observed (discovered-from: WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4).
- WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B — "Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin" (completed); the scheduler feature where the original Jul-12 corruption was first discovered.
- WL-0MLARH59Q0FY64WN — "TuiController Class" (completed); TUI refactor work, tangentially related context.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — ephemeral JSONL + SQLite architecture (sync flow context).

### Related work (automated report)

Automated findings from find_related (WL-0MS99Y6R40028Q9G): WL-0MRIEPH3J006RAPL (wl sync corrupts dev branch from worktree), WL-0MLARH59Q0FY64WN (TuiController Class), WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B (periodic request scheduling).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: No interactive interview was required — the work item already contained problem, evidence, workaround, and suggested investigation; the intake phase consisted of verifying and completing the investigation.
  - Answer: (agent/Map) Completed root-cause analysis. Source: live reproduction + repo inspection, 2026-08-01.
- Q (research): "What exactly happens when the post-checkout hook runs `wl sync` in a worktree?"
  - Answer (agent/Map): Confirmed by reproduction in a throwaway worktree at /tmp (branch `traceA`): the hook env contains `GIT_DIR=<worktree-gitdir>` (git does not unset it for the hook's grandchildren), which leaks into `withTempWorktree()`'s `git -C <tmp>/wt ...` commands, redirecting index/HEAD operations to the user's worktree. This produces the destructive commit (parent = user HEAD, tree = only `.worklog/`) and a rejected push. Evidence: commits `71ed5ad1`, `bfb7b67a`, `cf779f70`, `1ce8fdff` (all orphaned/removed after repro); hook trace in `/tmp/hook-trace.log` (removed); original orphans `0509caaa`, `b772812d`, `5bdf6ce1` still inspectable via `git cat-file`.
- Q (research): "Why is the main checkout unaffected?"
  - Answer (agent/Map): In the main checkout `hasRemote=true` (data ref exists), so `run()` never takes the `git rm -r` path; only the JSONL is staged/committed. The historical `dev` corruption (`af3388f`, Jul 12) was the pre-guard bug already fixed (WL-0MQRBT8BS00355AB / WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0).
- Q (research): "Does the pre-push hook already handle worktrees?"
  - Answer (agent/Map): Yes — `.githooks/pre-push` skips when `git-dir != git-common-dir` and for `*tmp-worktree-*` PWDs (WL-0MRIFWG8O005CLI0). Post-checkout/post-pull hooks lack the same guard — the gap this item closes.
- Q (research): "Should hooks skip worktrees, or should wl sync be fixed instead?"
  - Answer (agent/Map): Both. Hooks skipping worktrees is the primary fix (sync is only meaningful from an initialized worklog location, and worktrees are for feature work; matches pre-push precedent). Clearing `GIT_*` env in `withTempWorktree` is defense-in-depth that also fixes manual `wl sync` in worktrees and temp-worktree cleanup failures. No OPEN QUESTIONS remain.

# Intake Brief: auto-retry on 'Provider finish_reason: error'

## Problem statement

When a streaming model call ends with an error `finish_reason`, pi-ai's `mapStopReason` (in `pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js`) returns `{ stopReason: "error", errorMessage: "Provider finish_reason: <reason>" }`. The Worklog TUI extension's recovery module classifies the resulting assistant message and retries retryable categories — but the message `'Provider finish_reason: error'` (finish_reason === "error", e.g. proxy Tier-1 retry exhaustion on remote streaming stalls) matches **no** error pattern and falls through to `ErrorCategory.UNKNOWN`, which notifies without retrying. The user must manually retry, losing partial work.

## Users

- **Pi users whose LLM provider terminates a stream with finish_reason "error"** (transient stalls via local proxy / opencode-go / deepseek-v4-flash).
  - *As a user, I want the session to automatically retry when the provider ends the stream with finish_reason: error, so that I don't lose progress or have to manually intervene.*
  - *As a user, I want to understand why a retry happened, so I trust that the system is handling transient issues gracefully.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an assistant error message contains `Provider finish_reason: error`, the recovery module classifies it as a retryable category (TIMEOUT, consistent with the 'Stream ended without finish_reason' precedent) and triggers the automatic retry loop with exponential backoff.
2. The error pattern(s) are added to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS` in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`, conservatively (specific to finish_reason: error; must NOT match the existing content_filter or network_error cases, which are already handled as TERMINATED / TIMEOUT).
3. A test in `error-classification.test.ts` verifies that `Provider finish_reason: error` is classified as retryable (not UNKNOWN), and that the existing `content_filter` → TERMINATED and `network_error` → TIMEOUT classifications still hold (no regression).
4. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Must not add new npm dependencies — pattern addition only.
- Must not modify the retry loop engine, classification dispatch, or recovery module registration — only the error patterns in `error-patterns.ts` and their tests.
- Pattern must be conservative and specific to avoid false-positive matches on unrelated errors.
- Existing behavior for `content_filter` (TERMINATED, no retry) and `network_error` (TIMEOUT, retry) must be preserved.

## Existing state

- The recovery module lives at `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/`.
- `mapStopReason` in `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js` (lines ~930-951) produces three finish_reason error variants:
  - `content_filter` → matches `/content.filter/i` → TERMINATED (no retry, correct)
  - `network_error` → matches `/network\s*error/i` → TIMEOUT (retried, correct)
  - default catch-all `Provider finish_reason: <reason>` (e.g. "error") → matches NO pattern → UNKNOWN → no retry
- Verified by regex test against current `DEFAULT_*_PATTERNS`: `'Provider finish_reason: error'` matches none of the 7 category pattern sets.

## Desired change

1. Add a regex pattern (e.g. `/finish_reason\s*:\s*error/i` and/or a `Provider finish_reason` prefix variant) to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS` in `error-patterns.ts`, capturing `Provider finish_reason: error` and similar variants.
2. Add a test case in `error-classification.test.ts` confirming the new pattern matches and classifies as `ErrorCategory.TIMEOUT` (retryable).
3. Add regression assertions that `Provider finish_reason: content_filter` still classifies TERMINATED and `Provider finish_reason: network_error` still classifies TIMEOUT.
4. Verify no regressions in existing timeout/terminated classification tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — add pattern(s) to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_PATTERNS`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-classification.test.ts` — add/update classification tests
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — dispatch site (reference only; no changes expected)
- `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js` — reference only: origin of the error message (`mapStopReason`, lines ~930-951); do not modify (pi-ai is a dependency)

## Related work

- **WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4** (completed) — 'retry Error: Stream ended without finish_reason': identical classification-gap fix; established the pattern-addition + test approach and TIMEOUT mapping. This item is the direct precedent.
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** — parent work item that established the recovery/retry module ('Automatically recover from appropriate server errors').
- **SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW** (SorraAgents worklog, deleted) — the originating client-side follow-up; this item supersedes it with a concrete, repo-specific fix.
- **LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C** — RCA for occasional 'Provider finish_reason: error' from remote streaming stalls (tracked in another project's worklog).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** finish_reason "error" is transient and retryable. If the provider consistently errors, retries will not help and the existing UNKNOWN diagnostic path remains the fallback.
- **Risk:** Overly broad pattern (e.g. matching any 'finish_reason: X') could reclassify errors that should be terminal. Mitigate: match only the specific 'error' value (and optionally the 'Provider finish_reason' prefix) so content_filter/network_error handling is untouched.
- **Risk:** The retry loop does not re-execute completed tool calls (existing engine behavior); no new tool-call handling is introduced in this change.
- **Scope-creep risk:** If partial-content merge semantics are later desired (retry-and-append vs. diagnostic), track as a separate follow-up work item rather than expanding this pattern-only fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should this be in the Pi client (pi-ai / pi-coding-agent) or ContextHub? — Answer (user): Create the work item in ContextHub with all available detail and the proposed fix; the recovery module (which owns retry behavior) lives there. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: Which error category should 'Provider finish_reason: error' map to? — Answer (assumption, documented): TIMEOUT, consistent with the precedent WL-0MR4WJRGA00536X4 ('Stream ended without finish_reason' → TIMEOUT) since the failure mode is a mid-stream stall. Source: precedent work item + pi-ai source inspection.
- Q: Verified classification of existing variants — `Provider finish_reason: content_filter` → TERMINATED (patterns /content.filter/i, /content_filter/i); `Provider finish_reason: network_error` → TIMEOUT (pattern /network\s*error/i); `Provider finish_reason: error` → UNKNOWN (no match). Source: regex test against current DEFAULT_*_PATTERNS.

## Summary

`wl sync` can merge one project's worklog data into another project's database and push it to the wrong project's remote `refs/worklog/data`. This occurs when `wl sync` is invoked with `--worklog-dir` from a working directory inside a *different* git repository.

## Evidence

Investigation found this exact mechanism in production:

- `Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/logs/sync.log` at `2026-08-01T12:15:14Z` shows a sync with:
  - `file=/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (cwd-based data path)
  - Local state: 2014 work items (TCE's clean DB, via `--worklog-dir`)
  - Remote state: 2109 work items (ContextHub's remote worklog ref)
- The merge wrote `2014 + 2109 = 4123` items into the TCE DB and pushed the polluted data to `origin refs/worklog/data` (commit `7dd8a920`, +11131 lines).
- SorraAgents was polluted the same way (`2026-08-01T14:25Z`).
- Every project DB now contains a full copy of the core ContextHub worklog (2117 WL- items incl. 523 deleted) — see the cleanup work item `related-to:WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3`.

## Root cause

Two defects combine:

1. **`cli.ts` resolves the `-f/--file` default before the `--worklog-dir` override is applied.** `createPluginContext(program)` calls `getDefaultDataPath()` → `resolveWorklogDir()` at CLI startup based on the inherited process cwd. The `--worklog-dir` override is only applied later in the `preAction` hook (`cli.ts:203-205`). So `--worklog-dir <proj>/.worklog` redirects the DB, log file, and push target to the project — but the `-f` default (used by `sync.ts` `getRemoteDataFileContent(options.file, gitTarget)` for the remote fetch) still points at the cwd's repo.

2. **herdr's auto-sync spawns `wl sync` without a `cwd`** (`packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` `runSync` → `spawn('wl', ['--worklog-dir', worklogDir, 'sync', ...])`). The child inherits the herdr pane's cwd, which can be inside a different repo than the tab's resolved worklog dir (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`).

Net effect of `wl sync --worklog-dir <TCE>/.worklog` run from a ContextHub-repo cwd:
- DB / log / push target → TCE (override) — correct
- remote fetch → `git show <ContextHub's refs/worklog/data>:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` (cwd's repo) — WRONG project's data
- merged result (union, no prefix filter) is written to TCE's DB and pushed to TCE's remote

## User stories

- As a user running `wl sync` in any project, I expect sync to only ever read from and write to my own project's worklog data.
- As a maintainer, I expect `--worklog-dir`, `-f/--file`, and the git repo context to always refer to the same project.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Apply the `--worklog-dir` override before computing `ctx.dataPath` (move `createPluginContext` after the override is applied, or compute the `-f` default inside the action after the override is set).
- Add a safety guard: when `--worklog-dir` is set and the resolved remote data path belongs to a different git repo than cwd, fail loudly instead of merging.
- Make herdr's `runSync` pass `cwd` rooted at the tab's worklog project (and/or pass `-f` explicitly) so spawned `wl sync` always operates on the tab project.
- Optionally, filter merged items by the configured project prefix as a defense-in-depth guard.

## Related work items

- `discovered-from:WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` (self)
- `related-to:WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` (wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes spawned by worklist pane auto-sync)
- `related-to:WL-0MSAH2A71000MUA3` (cleanup of already-polluted project DBs)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl sync --worklog-dir <proj>/.worklog` run from inside a different git repo either syncs only the target project's data or fails with a clear error; it never merges foreign-prefix items.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: dataPath resolution order with `--worklog-dir`; herdr auto-sync spawning with correct `cwd`; a guard test proving no cross-project merge is possible.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; no regressions in normal `wl sync` flows (no flags, `--worklog-dir` only, `-f` only).
- [ ] The original failing scenario is reproduced in a test and fixed.
**Key Files:**

- `src/cli.ts` — `createPluginContext` runs at module load (line ~236) before the `preAction` hook applies the `--worklog-dir` override (lines ~200-205); fix the resolution order here.
- `src/cli-utils.ts` — `createPluginContext` computes `ctx.dataPath` via `getDefaultDataPath()`; must reflect the override.
- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — `setWorklogDirOverride` / `resolveWorklogDir` (override bypasses cwd/git resolution).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — `getDefaultDataPath()` (`path.join(resolveWorklogDir(), 'worklog-data.jsonl')`).
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — `-f/--file` defaults to `dataPath` (line ~336); `getRemoteDataFileContent(options.file, ...)` fetches the remote from the cwd repo's ref.
- `src/sync.ts` — `getRemoteDataFileContent` resolves the relative path against the cwd repo root (`getRepoRoot()`).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` with `--worklog-dir` but no `cwd`; must pass the tab project's cwd.
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — reproduction + guard tests for dataPath resolution order and cross-project merge prevention.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.test.ts` — spawn `cwd` coverage.
